title: Preliminary Privacy Assessment — Telemetry Data Access Risk

fields.to: Administrator on Call (AOC), Information Security Officer (ISO), Public Information Officer (PIO)
fields.subject: Preliminary Privacy Assessment: Telemetry Server Access Risk from Unauthorized Vendor Session
fields.body:
This is the preliminary assessment of the privacy risk from the unauthorized session on ORRMC-VSB01 (203.0.113.77) at 13:48–13:58. The session scanned ORRMC-MON01 and attempted a connection to the telemetry server, which hosts patient names, MRNs, and waveform data for ICU 3 North, 3 South, 4 East, and 7 East.

No evidence has been found in the logs that data was read, copied, or exfiltrated. However, the system was not designed to prevent access to stored protected health information (PHI) during a session. The forensic hold on ORRMC-MON01 logs has been initiated and will be preserved for review.

Per 45 CFR 164.402, a ransomware incident involving encrypted PHI is treated as a presumptive breach unless the risk assessment shows a low probability of compromise. The discovery time of the incident is confirmed as 14:40 (from I-03), and I have begun the four-factor risk assessment as required.

I will not issue a final determination until the forensic firm has analyzed the full log set, including the session timeline and memory dump from ORRMC-MON01. In the interim, no statement may claim that patient data was not accessed. The risk remains open.

This assessment is filed under CPO-2026-0312-004. All teams must defer disclosure until the CPO issues a formal risk conclusion.
fields.signatureBlock:
Joyce Tanaka
Chief Privacy Officer
Ottawa River Regional Medical Center

instructorNote: This inject triggers the HIPAA breach assessment process under C1. The CPO is now formally engaged; the AOC and ISO must preserve discovery time and not close the risk window. The PIO must not comment on data access until the CPO finalizes the assessment.
